capex_to_revenue.why: Capex ran at 0.1314 of revenue in 2025 and 0.0958 pooled over five years. Revenue is higher in 2026 and then falls, while nine-month additions of 11,671 point to roughly 15 billion a year, so about 0.11 of revenue is consistent over the five years.

fade_years.why: A commodity cycle and the loss of the price-driven margin take years to work through, and the record shows margins moving widely over a decade. A 10-year fade lets the margin reach the long-run level gradually.

long_run_op_margin.why: The 11-year margin record has a median of about 0.24 and ranges from -0.07 to 0.52. The base rate says an above-median cyclical margin retains perhaps half its gap over 5 to 10 years, which would be higher. I set the long-run margin at the median because high-price years such as 2022 and 2026 are not a durable level and depletion and the energy transition limit upside.

op_margin.why: Nine-month net operating income of 33,731 on revenue of 96,210 gives about 35%, so year 1 is set near 0.34. The margin then falls toward the median as prices normalise, following the base rate that a cyclical margin above its median keeps only part of the gap over time. Rising depreciation and recent impairments add some drag.

quotes.quote: Base year: return on tangible capital 0.1253
Return on new investment at which growth adds no value (code, after the company's leverage): 0.0547

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The base-year return on tangible capital is 12.5%, but this is a price-cycle-dependent figure and the tax take is very high. New investment is spread across lower-return power and international projects, so I use 10%, well above the 5.47% break-even level.

rev_growth.why: Year 1 (2026) is lifted by the oil and gas price spike: nine-month revenue is up 19% and Brent is up 33%, so a full-year rise near 20% is likely. Years 2 and 3 assume prices ease from about 94 toward a lower level, partly offset by 2026 production growth guided to about 4%. After that, growth is roughly flat to slightly positive as Norwegian shelf output is stable and international and power additions are modest.

quotes.quote: Cost of equity r 0.0841; long-run nominal growth anchor g_anchor 0.0375

terminal_growth.why: This is a mature producer on a depleting shelf, with limited volume growth beyond new fields and power additions, so I use 2%, below the 3.75% nominal anchor. Long-run growth is mostly price inflation, and the portfolio is slowly shifting toward power.

risks.risk: Oil and gas prices fall back faster and further than assumed, and the margin reverts to a low-price level
Revenue falls more steeply after the 2026 price spike
Depletion and energy-transition pressure cap long-run growth
New investment, including power assets, earns close to its cost of capital after the very high tax take

debt_level_representative.why: Gross debt of about 30 billion is similar to a year earlier, but net debt to capital employed adjusted fell from 17.8% to 3.8% on high-price cash flow, so the long-run level depends on prices and payouts.

situation.margin_position: The filed 2025 margin of 0.2381 sits at the 11-year median. The 2026 margin is well above it: nine-month net operating income of 33,731 on revenue of 96,210 is about 35%. Brent averaged 94.0 against 70.9 a year earlier, and European piped gas reached 16.17 USD/mmbtu. That is a commodity price spike, not a structural margin gain.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 71.5% rate reflects the petroleum tax regime on Norwegian Continental Shelf profits, and the interim effective rate on adjusted operating income of 70.8% to 71.4% is similar, so it looks sustainable while the Norwegian mix stays dominant.

situation.why: Equinor is an integrated oil and gas producer whose revenue and margin follow commodity prices, as the record swings from -0.0747 in 2020 to 0.5226 in 2022 show. The 2025 base year was a mid-cycle, lower-price year, and 2026 is a high-price year with revenue up 19% for nine months. Year 1 should therefore step up sharply, then drift back toward the median as prices normalise. A very high tax take of about 71% on petroleum profits caps what reaches shareholders.

quotes.quote: Deferral of production to create future value, gas off-take, timing of new capacity coming on stream and operational regularity

fade_years.why: Ten years reflects that new capacity and projects (Bay du Nord, Bacalhau, Adura) shift the asset base gradually rather than all at once. The company's own outlook flags timing of new capacity as a key risk.

long_run_op_margin.why: The 11-year filed history runs from negative to 52%, with a median near 24%. For a commodity company, the margin above median in 2026 should keep roughly half its gap over time. A mid-cycle price and higher depreciation point to about 21%, a bit under the median.

op_margin.why: Nine-month 2026 operating margin is about 35% (Q3 net operating income of 11,955 on 33,190), so year 1 is about 34%. It fades toward the long-run level as prices normalise. Rising depreciation (12,318 in 2025) and impairments weigh on margins at lower prices.

quotes.quote: Return on new investment at which growth adds no value (code, after the company's leverage): 0.0547

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: Base-year return on tangible capital is 12.5% after a 71% tax rate, and growth adds no value at 5.5%. New investment is diversifying into power (low or negative current margins), so I assume a return of about 9%, below the current level but above breakeven.

rev_growth.why: Year 1 (2026) revenue is far above 2025 because of price: nine-month revenue is up 19% and Brent averaged 94.0 against 70.9. I assume prices ease from Q3 levels, so revenue falls in years 2 and 3. After that, growth is roughly flat to low as ~4% production growth in 2026 fades and NCS output stays stable.

terminal_growth.why: A mature integrated oil and gas producer with a stable NCS and a transition toward power should grow below the 3.75% nominal anchor. I use 2%, about inflation, since the evidence shows volumes only offsetting decline in Norway.

risks.risk: Oil and gas prices fall back to 2025 levels or lower, so the 2026 margin spike does not persist and the mid-cycle margin is lower
Further impairments and production-profile cuts (as in Q3 2026 on a cross-border NCS asset) combined with unplanned outages lower margins in the near years
Price decline is sharper than assumed and NCS decline outpaces new fields, so revenue falls more in years 2 to 3

debt_level_representative.why: Total debt of 30,146 was raised in 2025, but net debt to capital employed has since fallen to 3.8% from 17.8%, so the 2025 level is probably higher than the company will carry at current prices.

situation.margin_position: The 2025 margin of 23.8% sits below the company's own 11-year median (about 0.24) and well below the 2021-2024 levels. Oil and gas prices were weak in 2025 and depreciation and impairments rose. 2026 is running far above that, with Brent at 94.0 for nine months and nine-month net operating income of 33,731 on 96,210 of revenue (about 35%). The 2026 margin is a price spike, not a base to extrapolate.

tax_rate_representative.why: The 71.5% base-year rate is driven by Norwegian petroleum taxation on the NCS, and the nine-month 2026 rate on adjusted operating income was 70.8%, so it looks sustainable while NCS dominates the earnings mix.

situation.why: 2025 was a low-price year with high impairments, and 2026 revenue and margins are sharply higher because of price. Neither year is a mid-cycle level. I forecast a spike in year 1 that mean-reverts toward a margin near the long-run median, not the 2022 peak.

risks.basis: stated in F2 and P1; the link between impairments and future earnings is inferred
risks.claim: Impairment and depreciation charges are rising and can reduce operating income further. risks.basis: stated in the outlook text; the possibility of a cut is inferred
risks.claim: The raised 2026 production guide depends on operational regularity and other factors the company names as risks, and unplanned losses at Johan Castberg and Troll already occurred in Q3.
quotes: Deferral of production to create future value, gas off-take, timing of new capacity coming on stream and operational regularity and levels of industry product supply, demand and pricing represent the most significant risks related to the foregoing production guidance.
New fields, such as Halten East and Verdande, and contribution from new wells offset natural decline and unplanned losses from Johan Castberg and Troll.

risks.basis: stated in the release; the effect on earnings is inferred
risks.claim: Results and cash flow depend on realised prices and geopolitical conditions. Management credits higher prices for part of the Q3 2026 result, and the outlook warns that prices, policy and macro conditions will affect cash flow and liquidity.
quotes: High production in the third quarter enabled us to capture additional value from higher prices.

Our future financial performance, including cash flow and liquidity, will be affected by geopolitical and macroeconomic conditions, changes in the regulatory and policy landscape, the development in realised prices, including price differentials, tolls and tariffs and other factors discussed elsewhere in the report.

risks.basis: tax and pre-tax figures are stated; the regulatory risk is inferred
